answer: The admission burn is multiplied by 2 for each member already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival burns the most. The zephyr multiplier is published, charged in relic, and vine lists each payment. A burst of registrations therefore prices itself out, since the marginal alias costs more than the first by design. A farm of 1032 identities would post 1801 proofs and burn roughly 15 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. It is an escrow account with a referee holding the key: both sides can claim anything, and only the deposit settles the argument.
